newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Dutch closing debt market report.
newsitem.headline: Dutch closing debt market report.

text.p: Dutch bonds rallied at the close after sharp morning losses as the European Union's heads of government reached agreement on an EMU stability pact.
"People were waiting for news of the stability pact in Dublin," one trader said.
Dutch bonds themselves, though following the German and U.S. lead, were thinly traded, the dips attracting few buyers and very little institutional interest.
"It's really just professionals out there, selling long positions. The surge at the end was a slight short squeeze," said a trader before news of the stability pact emerged.
However, few traders were convinced that the gains represented more than a short-term bounce.
"We did not predict this upturn. Based on technicals, we should be heading down," one trader said.

Spreads under bunds widened during the morning weakness. Towards the close, however, Dutch bonds closely tracked the bund and bund futures gains, unlike their higher yielding government bond counterparts. Bund spreads were unchanged at the close.
The stability relative to bunds, gave professionals few options but to switch among maturities along a volatile curve.
